gloss: resumptive of a preposed complement (唯利是視 -> 利を是れ視る)

possessive/attributive particle. The empty `okurigana` is what puts の over the character rather than beside it: KundokuView.ts reads an entry that states an okurigana of its own as a split — a reading of the character (furigana) plus an ending (okurigana slot) — the same shape 以 takes as もつ+て and 毎 as ごと+に, and an entry with no okurigana at all as one gloss standing in for the character, which goes in the okurigana slot entire. の is a reading of 之 and not a gloss standing in for it (KANJIDIC2 lists の first among its kun'yomi), so it takes the furigana slot, with nothing following it. Empty rather than absent is the whole of the difference, and it moves the annotation slot only: `spellOutInProse` still writes 酒の精 in the 書き下し文, never 酒之精

possessive/attributive particle (X之Y = Y's X, e.g. 少典之子 -> 少典の子). Kept as a dep-keyed entry alongside the ADP/PART one above because the two answer different parses of the same use: 0.3.0 tagged the genitive SCONJ and only this entry reached it, while 0.3.1's `lzh_upos_rules` repairs it to PART from the head's category and the entry above reaches it too. Verified against the shipped 0.3.1 wheel: 少典之子 comes out mod/PART, so both entries match and both give の. This one still earns its place — the repair keys on the head, so a head the parser reads as a verb leaves the genitive SCONJ (酒之精 parses that way in isolation), and this is what answers then. Empty `okurigana` for the same reason as the ADP/PART entry above — see its gloss: it puts の over the character instead of beside it, and changes nothing in the prose

the subject genitive — 之 standing between a clause's subject and its predicate, which nominalises the clause: 人之不己知 is 人**の**己を知らざる, "people's not knowing one", and 禮之用 is 禮**の**用. The same word and the same reading as the attributive `mod` entry above; what differs is only which side of 之 the parser hangs the phrase from, and it hangs it from the *predicate* here, so the relation comes back `subj` instead. **451 tokens** over the kanbun.info corpus's own parses (SCONJ 332, PART 99, PRON 20) against 56 genuinely resumptive `comp@expl`, and without this entry every one of them fell through to the char-only これ and read 禮**を之れ**用ゐる. Empty `okurigana` for the reason the two entries above carry it — see the ADP/PART entry's gloss: it puts の over the character instead of beside it
one who... (nominalizer; は when 者 is instead modified by a bare noun/name — see readingResolver.ts's zheTopicReading)

the 提示 也 — the one that marks a topic rather than closing a predicate, read や: 其為人也孝弟 is 其の人と為るや孝弟なり, 由也好勇 is 由や勇を好む, 今也則亡 is 今や則ち亡し. **The list is every relation that is not `discourse`/`discourse@sp`, and it is long because this 也 has no role of its own: it *heads the phrase it marks*, so it wears whatever role that phrase plays.** Measured over the recoded gold — of the ~440 non-discourse 也, 246 govern one dependent, 141 two and 25 three, and only 4 govern nothing; what they govern is the topic itself (416 `comp:obj`), and what they hang off is the main predicate (VERB 254, ADJ 81, AUX 37). 由也好勇 is the shape: 也 governs 由 as `comp:obj` and attaches to 好 as `subj`. The assertive 也 is the mirror image — `discourse@sp` 7,317 times, and **6,059 of those govern nothing at all**, a bare particle on the predicate — which is why the division is drawn on the relation and not on a list of roles. Position needs no clause here and is already right: a 也 standing last is routed to both panels' discourse branch by `isSentenceFinalParticleUse`'s positional fallback, before this table is consulted, so the 9 gold tokens that carry a topic relation *and* close their sentence (丑見王之敬子也) keep their なり, as do the 8 sentence-final `ROOT` ones (`conlluParser.ts` normalises a lowercase `root` DEPREL to `ROOT`, which is the spelling this list has to use). **The や it produces must not bind a 連体形**: it is declarative, not the interrogative や of 乎/歟, and 係り結び is the interrogative's. That falls out rather than being asserted — `closingParticleReading` consults the reading resolver only for a `discourse`/`discourse@sp` particle, so a 提示 也 never reaches `BINDING_PARTICLE_READINGS` at all

sentence-final copula/assertion (this entry does not decide how 也 is annotated: at dep discourse/discourse@sp both panels take the reading from SENTENCE_FINAL_PARTICLES in bungoConjugation.ts instead, and put it in the okurigana slot outright — see the discourse branch in KundokuView.ts and generator.ts. Splitting this entry cannot move なり into the furigana slot; that has to be done in those branches)

at/in/to (locative particle, = 於 and 乎). The third spelling of the one postposition, and given the entry its two fellows already had: 乎 has carried an ADP -> に entry all along and 於 is answered by `yuParts` in conjugationContext.ts, while 于 reached neither and printed as a bare character — 于 stood where the received reading has に **19** times over the kanbun.info corpus. に and not より for the reason `yuParts`' own note gives: the postposition is a 置き字 marking place, time or goal, and より is the comparison

in, at (locative modifier: 於日中俯臥 -> 日中に於いて俯臥せしむ). The split is お + いて, not おい + て. KANJIDIC2 lists both boundaries for this one character — おい.て (= 於て) and お.ける (= 於ける) — and the second is the one to follow: 於いて and 於ける are the same stem お-, so a boundary that moves between them is describing two different characters. 於いて is also the ordinary modern spelling of the phrase this entry glosses. NOTE: no parse reaches this entry, and it is kept as the statement of record about how the character divides rather than as a lookup. `yuParts` in conjugationContext.ts answers for every token whose lemma is 於, and both panels consult it ahead of the override lookup, so 於 never arrives here — the strings live there, in the one place that also decides which of the two senses applies. That decision is NOT this entry's `contextDep`: 取之於藍's 於 wears `mod@lmod` exactly as 坐於堂's does (measured), so the sense is taken from the governing verb (`LOCATIVE_GOVERNOR_LEMMAS`) and a dep-keyed rule read 藍に於いて取る. The two older 於 entries that stood here — contextPos ADP -> に, and a char-only において — were removed with this note: unreachable for the same reason, absent from the historical-kana transfer table (`historicalKana.ts` skips any entry whose modern spelling is its own), and both stating a reading this app has decided against. に is now what 於's *object* takes (`caseParticleFor`), not what the character reads. 乎's own ADP -> に entry is untouched and stays live: nothing short-circuits that character

to be like — 聖と仁との若きは. Divided ごと + し, exactly as the 如 entry above is, and as the received text writes it (若き, 若く, 若し). The entry does not conjugate, so the し stands where an inflected form belongs; that is unchanged by the division and is a separate want

from, following (从 is 從's simplified form and KANJIDIC2 gives it the same three kun'yomi, したが.う / したが.える / より — but より is the third of them and undotted, and an ADP reaches neither of pickKun's two preferences: it is not VERB/ADJ, so the dotted-first rule does not apply, and it is not NOUN/PRON, so the bare-kun rule does not either. The mixed bucket takes kun[0], したが.う, and 从 read したがふ where the postposition is より. Stated here for the same reason 從's own entry is, and beside it)

from, by way of (由 as a postposition is より — 由此觀之, "looking at it from this". KANJIDIC2 lists 由 as よし and よ.る and nothing else, so no lookup produces より for it at all: an ADP fell to kun[0] and read よし, the noun "reason". The character's ADV entry below is a different word again (なほ, "still, yet"), which is why this one names the ADP slot rather than standing char-only)

to be like. Split ごと + し rather than written whole in the okurigana slot: ごと is what the character says and し is the adjective's own ending, the same division 以 takes as もつ + て and 毎 as ごと + に. KundokuView.ts keys the furigana slot off an entry stating an okurigana of its own, so this is what draws 如[ごと|シ] instead of 如[|ゴトシ]; the 書き下し文 goes on printing ごとし in kana either way

with, by means of, in order to (a split reading: もつ is the character's own reading and goes over it, て is the ending beside it. Spelled もつて rather than the modern もって — this app is written in 歴史的仮名遣い throughout, and 以て descends from もちて, so there is no small っ)
then, in that case (ADV-only: 則 is also the noun のり "rule, norm" — 有物有則 came out すなはち)

the sentence-final 助字, read as **nothing at all** — a 置き字, as 矣 is. **561** of the gold's 764 焉 stand on `discourse@sp` and a further 24 elsewhere as PART; this entry has said "" for them since it was written and was simply not reachable, so the character was taking KANJIDIC2's り instead — the 完了の助動詞 (て + あり), which attaches to a 四段已然形 and to nothing else, and which the particle branch was writing after a 終止形 (思ふり), a negation (在らずり) and a 連体形 (有るり) alike. It was never a reading of the character in any of its uses. The two other uses are the entries below: the interrogative adverb (96) and the fused 於之 pronoun (83)

how, why (rhetorical, = 安/惡) — 擇不處仁，焉得知 -> 焉んぞ知を得ん, 斯焉取斯 -> 斯れ焉んぞ斯を取らん. **Split いづ + くんぞ**, which is where the received text divides it — 焉くんぞ 18 times in the gold's own 書き下し文 and 焉くにか 3, against no 焉んぞ at all — and the division has to be *some* division for a second reason, downstream: `isInterrogativeBinder` reads the resolver's whole answer, furigana *plus* okurigana, and the 安 and 惡 entries this one joins carry the ぞ in the okurigana slot for exactly that reason. **96** gold tokens — ADV on `mod` 95, on `subj` 1 (夫焉有所倚) — out of 764 焉 in all, against 585 PART and 83 PRON. Without an entry the character fell to KANJIDIC2 and came back **いずくんぞ**, in modern kana where every other reading this app writes is 歴史的仮名遣い, and `INTERROGATIVE_BINDING_READINGS` in conjugationContext.ts has had to hold that modern spelling beside いづくんぞ to go on recognising the binder at all — a wart its own note names. No dep condition: an interrogative adverb is the interrogative wherever it stands, and the particle and the pronoun are answered by the entries on either side of this one

there, in it — the fused 於之, 心焉在 -> 心ここに在らず. **83** gold tokens: `udep` 55 (年四十而見惡焉), `comp:obj` 21 (二女女焉), `mod@lmod` 5, `subj` 1, `comp:obl@lmod` 1. Split ここ + に on the model of 為's ため + に and 於's お + いて, and for the same reason twice over: に is the 於 half of the fusion rather than part of the word, so it belongs beside the character and not over it — and **the split is what keeps a second particle off the token**. `ownReadingSuppliesCaseParticle` withholds the case particle of any closed-class token whose curated reading has already written one, so the を that `comp:obj` would otherwise put on those 21 goes unwritten, which is the right answer and not merely a tidy one: 焉 is 於之, and its slot is locative and never accusative. **Half of a pair, and inert until the other half lands.** `isSentenceFinalParticleUse` excludes a NOUN and a PROPN from the sentence-final particle it claims by position but not yet a PRON, so a PRON 焉 standing last is still routed to the discourse branch and read as nothing before this entry is ever consulted; the POS gate is conjugationContext.ts's to add

and, with (**ADP beside CCONJ**: the coordinating/comitative 與 is tagged `v,前置詞,関係,*` ADP by this parser, not CCONJ. Over the recoded gold (lzh_kyoto-sud-{train,dev,test}.relabeled_ext.udep_ruled.punct.rulemerged.adjfix.conllu) 與 is ADP **1,406** times — 663 mod, 325 cc, 131 comp:obl, 91 root, 68 mod@lmod, 47 conj:coord, 43 subj and a tail — and CCONJ **0**, so the CCONJ-only entry was unreachable on live output and 子罕言利與命與仁 came out 利あたえる命, the modern KANJIDIC2 kun あた.える standing where と belongs. CCONJ is kept beside ADP rather than replaced: it costs nothing at 0 gold tokens and a hand-corrected tree can still say it. The comitative and the coordinating use are one reading — 與民同樂 is 民と樂しみを同じくす, 利與命 is 利と命と — so no dep condition divides them)

question particle (= 歟/欤) (や, not か: 與 is also in SENTENCE_FINAL_PARTICLES in bungoConjugation.ts, and that is the entry both panels actually reach — they take the discourse branch before the resolver is consulted at all, so this one is only reachable for a 與 tagged something other than discourse/discourse@sp. Kept in step with that table rather than deleted, so the two cannot give one character two readings from two places — the same repair 歟's entry above got. か is NOT gone from the app and this gloss no longer claims it is: at the reader's instruction it is in GENUINE_QUESTION_PARTICLES beside SENTENCE_FINAL_PARTICLES, which is the one place a particle's second reading lives, and from there the furigana menu offers it and a 與 closing a 豈 clause reads it (曰：「豈謂是與？ -> 曰く「あに是を謂ふか」と). It is not restored HERE because this entry decides neither reading — the discourse branch never reaches it — so a か written back into it would print nowhere and would only be somewhere for the two answers to drift apart. や remains the default, and over the recoded gold it is what 187 of the 189 sentence-final 與 get)

to give (與ふ, ハ行下二段 — 與へ / 與へ / 與ふ / 與ふる / 與ふれ / 與へよ. **This entry states the reading and no longer the ending.** It is a fixed ふ, and every entry in this table is returned `endingComplete` and `spellOutInProse`, so a VERB 與 printed the bare kana あたふ in every syntactic position and the character never reached the prose at all — 乎諸其鄰而與之 came out これをあたふ where kundoku writes これに與へ. `verbLexicon.ts`'s RESIDUAL now holds 與/与 as 下二段ハ行 あた, and both panels reach that ahead of this table (`lexiconEntryFor`), so the paradigm is written there and the reading here is the same あた either way. Kept rather than deleted because it is still what the furigana menu offers for the character and what the resolver answers for a 與 the lexicon gate does not admit; the two cannot disagree about the reading, which is the only thing both state)

with, together with (adverbial 與/与 — 與(とも)に, the comitative standing as a bare adverb rather than as the ADP taking a complement, which is the と entry beside this one. 可與言 is 與に言ふべし; 未可與適道 is いまだ與に道に適くべからず; 揖所與立 is 與に立つところに揖す. **`beatsLexicon`, and it has to be.** This parser tags the adverbial 與 ADV with `VerbForm=Conv`, which `isConverbUse` admits to `usesLexiconEntry` — so the 下二段ハ行 與ふ "to give" `verbLexicon.ts` holds for the verb reached these tokens too and wrote 與へ on them: the right character conjugated as the wrong word. Exactly the 果 case that flag's own doc describes, and the reason an ADV entry needs the flag here where most do not. **Measured** over `lzh_kyoto-sud-{train,dev,test}.relabeled_ext.udep_ruled.punct.rulemerged.adjfix.conllu`: 與 is ADV **61** times, every one of them `v,動詞,行為,交流` on `mod` with `VerbForm=Conv`, and every one comitative — there is no second adverbial sense for an entry keyed on the tag to run over. Before this they printed 與えるて, KANJIDIC2's modern あた.える with a converb て glued on, which is a reading of nothing. **The word is stated whole here and divided by `KANJI_RETAINED_ADVERBS`** (classicalEnding.ts), which is where this app's divisions of a retained adverb live — 豈 as あに + に and 固 as もと + より — so that the split the prose panel prints, the split the 訓読文 draws and the split the furigana menu offers come from one table. It was written here as とも + に, on the model of 其 そ + の and 毎 ごと + に, and that division is unchanged on the page: に is the adverbial particle and sits beside the character, とも is the character's own reading — KANJIDIC2 lists it, undotted — and goes over it. What changed is which table says so. **And this entry is no longer what reaches the page**: with the character in that table the kanji survives into the prose, 可與言 as 與に言ふべし rather than ともに言ふべし, and the reading is drawn over 與 as furigana instead of standing beside it in the okurigana lane with the character bare. Kept, as the VERB entry above it is kept, because it is still what the furigana menu offers for the character and what the resolver answers for a 與 the retained-adverb gate does not admit; the two cannot disagree about the reading, which is the only thing both state)

to be, to serve as (copula-like predicate)

for the sake of; because of; by (passive agent) — 為人謀而不忠乎 -> 人の爲に謀りて忠ならざるか. **Split ため + に, not written whole**, on the model of 於's お + いて a few entries above: ため is what the character itself is read as and goes over it, に is the case particle completing the phrase and sits beside it in the okurigana slot, so the 訓読文 draws 為(ため)ニ and not 為(ためニ). An entry that states an `okurigana` of its own is exactly that claim — a reading of the character plus an ending — and one with no okurigana is a single gloss standing in for it, which goes in the okurigana slot entire (see KundokuView.ts, and 毎 as ごと + に). Nothing about the 書き下し文 moves: `spellOutInProse` writes reading + okurigana run together, which is ために either way. The reader's ruling; the の his object takes is `caseParticleFor`'s half of it and lives in conjugationContext.ts. Reached on the ADP tag alone, which is the parser's `v,前置詞,源泉,*`: over the gold 為/爲 is tagged ADP **1,045** times — 642 on `mod`, 138 on `root`, 90 on `comp:obl`, and a tail — against AUX 2,788 and VERB 1,656, which this entry does not touch (the copula たり entry above names VERB + comp:pred/ROOT, and the char-only なす below answers for the rest). **What it governs and what it modifies are two different edges, and only the first is its complement.** Those 1,045 tokens take **1,045** `comp:obj` dependents between them — NOUN 430, PROPN 217, PRON 210, VERB 132, ADJ 23, and a tail of PART 16, AUX 9, SCONJ 6, ADV 2 — and that is the phrase 爲 is the sake *of*, where every particle this construction writes goes: の after a common or proper noun (人の爲に謀る), が after a pronoun (我が爲に) and が after a predicate on its 連体形 — **155** of those, VERB 132 + ADJ 23, 其の病める**が**爲なり. **The 43 VERB/ADJ dependents standing `mod` on it are a different edge and take nothing at all** — VERB **37** and ADJ **6**, against the 155. They are the **matrix clause**: in 迎貓，為其食田鼠也 the gold makes 為 the root, its `comp:obj` the reason (其食田鼠) and its `mod` the thing done for it (迎貓), and 介者不拜，為其拜而蓌拜 is the same shape. The two were once counted here as one population of VERB — 132 "with a further 37 on `mod`" — which they are not: a が on the second would read 貓を迎ふる**が**爲に其れ田鼠を食らふ and turn the sentence inside out. `isPurposiveWeiComplement` in conjugationContext.ts draws the same line from the other side of the edge

for the sake of; because of; by (passive agent) — 為人謀而不忠乎 -> 人の爲に謀りて忠ならざるか. **Split ため + に, not written whole**, on the model of 於's お + いて a few entries above: ため is what the character itself is read as and goes over it, に is the case particle completing the phrase and sits beside it in the okurigana slot, so the 訓読文 draws 為(ため)ニ and not 為(ためニ). An entry that states an `okurigana` of its own is exactly that claim — a reading of the character plus an ending — and one with no okurigana is a single gloss standing in for it, which goes in the okurigana slot entire (see KundokuView.ts, and 毎 as ごと + に). Nothing about the 書き下し文 moves: `spellOutInProse` writes reading + okurigana run together, which is ために either way. The reader's ruling; the の his object takes is `caseParticleFor`'s half of it and lives in conjugationContext.ts. Reached on the ADP tag alone, which is the parser's `v,前置詞,源泉,*`: over the gold 為/爲 is tagged ADP **1,045** times — 642 on `mod`, 138 on `root`, 90 on `comp:obl`, and a tail — against AUX 2,788 and VERB 1,656, which this entry does not touch (the copula たり entry above names VERB + comp:pred/ROOT, and the char-only なす below answers for the rest). **What it governs and what it modifies are two different edges, and only the first is its complement.** Those 1,045 tokens take **1,045** `comp:obj` dependents between them — NOUN 430, PROPN 217, PRON 210, VERB 132, ADJ 23, and a tail of PART 16, AUX 9, SCONJ 6, ADV 2 — and that is the phrase 爲 is the sake *of*, where every particle this construction writes goes: の after a common or proper noun (人の爲に謀る), が after a pronoun (我が爲に) and が after a predicate on its 連体形 — **155** of those, VERB 132 + ADJ 23, 其の病める**が**爲なり. **The 43 VERB/ADJ dependents standing `mod` on it are a different edge and take nothing at all** — VERB **37** and ADJ **6**, against the 155. They are the **matrix clause**: in 迎貓，為其食田鼠也 the gold makes 為 the root, its `comp:obj` the reason (其食田鼠) and its `mod` the thing done for it (迎貓), and 介者不拜，為其拜而蓌拜 is the same shape. The two were once counted here as one population of VERB — 132 "with a further 37 on `mod`" — which they are not: a が on the second would read 貓を迎ふる**が**爲に其れ田鼠を食らふ and turn the sentence inside out. `isPurposiveWeiComplement` in conjugationContext.ts draws the same line from the other side of the edge

not yet — 未だ. Divided いま + だ, the same division `REREAD_CHARACTERS` now makes for the 再読 use of the same character. Measured at exactly 0 over the gold, where every 未 is the 再読 use and reaches that table instead; stated here so that a 未 which is not read twice does not divide the one word differently

is not (negative copula). The reading is あら and the okurigana ず, which is what puts 非[あら|ズ] on the page rather than the whole アラズ beside a bare character: KundokuView.ts reads an entry that states an okurigana of its own as a split — a reading of the character in the furigana slot, an ending beside it — and an entry with no okurigana as one gloss standing in for the character, which goes in the okurigana slot entire (the same shape 毎 takes as ごと+に). あら is a reading of 非 and ず is the negation completing it, so they belong in the two slots. Nothing about the prose moves: `spellOutInProse` writes reading+okurigana, which is あらず either way (ADV-only: 非 is also the noun "wrong, fault", tagged NOUN — 是非之心 and 文過飾非 both came out あらず. Every negative-copula use checked (非其鬼而祭之, 人非生而知之者, 非我也) is ADV with Polarity=Neg)

to wish to, to want to (desiderative auxiliary) (left undivided deliberately: 歴史的仮名遣い has no small っ, so ほっす is respelled ほつす, but Wiktionary has no ほっす entry at all — it reads the spelling 欲す as a different verb, ほりす, and gives an okurigana boundary only for 欲する (ほっ + する). Rather than invent one, the whole gloss stays in the okurigana slot)

someone, a certain person (PRON: 或言蟲是劉之福 is "someone said the worm was Liu's good fortune", not "or". The char-only entry below reads あるいは, the disjunctive adverb, which is the right word for an ADV 或 and the wrong one for a subject — 或 standing as the subject of a speech verb is a person. Split あ + るひと, not written whole: the reading is a real word of the character's own, so あ goes over it as furigana and るひと beside it in the okurigana slot, which is what an entry that states its own okurigana asks for (see KundokuView.ts's note on the split, and 毎 as ごと+に). A PRON is the one POS whose override reading takes the furigana slot at all — see ResolvedReading.spellOutInProse — so the split reaches the page here and would not on an ADV. The 書き下し文 still writes the word out in kana as あるひと, as it does for every other pronoun in this table (之 これ, 其 それ)

someone; perhaps, maybe. Divided ある + いは — KANJIDIC2 files 或 as あ.る / あるい / あるいは, so the dot it states is あ.る, the verb, and the disjunctive adverb is the undotted あるいは; this app divides it after the stem the verb shares, which is where the received text puts it. 或いは stands 75 times in kanbun.info's prose and あるいは in kana none

although, even though (と…雖も — postposed after its own clause, with the と suffixed onto that clause's own last token, not onto 雖 itself — see reorderEngine.ts's quoteEndIds reuse; the parser tags it ADV as often as SCONJ, so this is unrestricted rather than context-gated)

its, that (attributive determiner — a split reading, the same one 以 takes as もつ+て and 乃 as すなは+ち: そ is the character's own reading and goes over it, の is the attributive particle and sits beside it as okurigana. 其の, not 其(その))
how could it be that... (rhetorical negation adverb)
only, merely — 唯だ仁者のみ. Divided た + だ, which the received text's 唯だ (12 times in the gold) forces: the word is ただ, so the kana beside the character can only be its second mora
only, merely (= 唯) (ADV-only: 惟 is also the verb おもんみる "to consider" — 思惟其事 came out ただその事を思ふ)
finally, in the end (ADV-only: 遂 is also the verb とぐ "to accomplish", tagged VERB — 其事遂矣 came out その事つひに)
then, immediately (= 乃; KANJIDIC writes its すなわち undivided)

then, thereupon (= 乃). ADV-gated for the same reason 則 is: 便 is also the noun たより "tidings, convenience", and its on'yomi ビン/ベン carries that sense too, so an unconditioned entry would claim those. 劉愕然、便求醫療 came out 便りて
therefore, for that reason (adverbial modifier — the parser doesn't always tag this CCONJ)

my (attributive: 吾日三省吾身 -> 吾れ日に吾が身を三省す, 啟予足 -> 予が足を啟け). **The relation is the rule.** A first-person pronoun standing `det` on a nominal is a genitive and reads わが; standing `subj` or `comp:obj` it is the pronoun itself and reads われ, which is what the `contextPos: ["PRON"]` entry beside this one goes on saying. The gold (`lzh_kyoto-sud-{train,dev,test}.relabeled_ext.udep_ruled.punct.rulemerged.adjfix.conllu`) divides the five characters **393 `det`** against **1,103 `subj`** and **401 `comp:obj`** — 吾 225/654/29, 我 108/308/268, 余 38/40/40, 朕 15/32/6, 予 7/69/58 — and `det` is a genitive in every one of them: its head is a NOUN 375 times, a PROPN 5, and the remaining 13 are VERB/ADJ/PART/PRON heads that are nominal in the same way (罪在朕躬, 啟予足). Split わ + が, not written whole, on the model of 其's そ + の two entries above — which is the *same construction*, an attributive determiner on `det`, and settles the shape here rather than leaving it to preference: わ is the character's own reading and goes over it as furigana, が is the attributive particle and sits beside it as okurigana, so the 訓読文 draws 吾(わ)が身 and not 吾(わが)身. A PRON is the one POS whose override reading takes the furigana slot at all (see `ResolvedReading.spellOutInProse`), so the split reaches the page here exactly as 其's does; the 書き下し文 writes the word out in kana as わが, as it does for every other pronoun in this table. **`det` is where this table can name the genitive, and not the only place the reading is one.** A pronoun standing as the complement of a prepositional 為 is a genitive in exactly the reader's sense — 子盍為我言之 is 子なんぞ**わ**がために之を言はざる — and it arrives on `comp:obj`, which is also the relation an ordinary object stands in (我を愛す, 401 first-person pronouns over the gold). So no `contextDep` written here can reach that slot without claiming those as well: what makes it a genitive is the **governor**, and a key on (character, POS, relation) holds no fact about another token. `purposiveGenitivePronounReading` in readingResolver.ts borrows this entry's `reading` for that slot alone — **29** gold tokens, 我 19, 余 7, 吾 2, 朕 1, and 予 none — taking the わ and *not* the が, which `caseParticleFor` has already written there (a pronoun under 為 takes が where a noun takes の), so the particle is on the page once. The other pronouns that slot reaches are already right and are left alone: 之 (92) これがために and 誰 (3) たれがために hold no `det` entry at all, and 何 (46) is excluded by its own particle rather than by a list — its `det` reading is なに + **の**, the determiner of 何の藥, and なにがために is right as it stands, 何が故に being the ordinary kundoku of this frame
my (attributive genitive on `det` — 我老彭 -> 我が老彭). Split わ + が on 其's そ + の model; the whole argument, the relation, and the gold counts are on the 吾 entry above
my (attributive genitive on `det` — 啟予足 -> 予が足を啟け). Split わ + が on 其's そ + の model; the whole argument, the relation, and the gold counts are on the 吾 entry above
my (attributive genitive on `det` — 捐余玦兮江中 -> 余が玦を江中に捐つ). Split わ + が on 其's そ + の model; the whole argument, the relation, and the gold counts are on the 吾 entry above

which, what kind of (attributive determiner — 何の藥, not 何(なに)藥). A split reading exactly as 其 takes for the same role: なに is the character's own reading and goes over it, の is the attributive particle and sits beside it as okurigana. Keyed on the dep rather than the POS because that is what the rule is about, and because `contextDep` outscores the bare `contextPos: ["PRON"]` entry below (2 against 1), which is what makes this the more specific match rather than a competing one

why (rhetorical) — 何ぞ甚だしき. Divided なん + ぞ, which is how the received text writes it (何ぞ 25 times in the gold). The ぞ is the 係助詞 the 結び answers to and belongs beside the character; `isInterrogativeBinder` reads furigana and okurigana joined, so it still recognises the binder

how, why (rhetorical) — 安くんぞ. Divided いづ + くんぞ and keeping its character, both of them following the two measured synonyms 焉 and 惡 rather than a count of its own: the gold holds no ADV 安 at all, so either change measures at exactly 0 there, and one word written three ways across three characters is the thing this avoids

how (rhetorical, = 安) — 惡くにか名を成さん. Divided いづ + くんぞ, the same word and the same division as 焉 above; the received text writes 惡くにか, and `isInterrogativeBinder` reads the two halves joined, so moving the boundary within the word leaves the 係り結び exactly where it was

probably; now, (sentence-initial) (PART-only: 蓋 is also the noun "lid, canopy" and the verb おしふ "to cover" — 車蓋 (NOUN) came out けだし. Every sentence-initial use checked (蓋有之矣, 蓋均無貧, 蓋將自其變者而觀之) is tagged PART/discourse)
already. Divided すで + に on KANJIDIC2's own dot (すで.に) and kept as a character in the prose for the reason 凡 is: the received text writes 既に 60 times against no すでに at all
about to, on the verge of
about to, on the verge of (= 将)

dare to; presumptuously. Kept as a character in the prose for the reason 凡 and 既 are: the received text writes 敢えて 77 times and あえて in kana none. The division あ + へて is KANJIDIC2's own dot (あ.えて), in this app's historical spelling

again, moreover. The た beside the character rather than over it, and stated here because KANJIDIC2 files 復 as an undotted また: the received text writes 復た 36 times and never a bare 復 in this sense. Same residue as 亦, whose ending is stated in `KANJI_RETAINED_ADVERBS` for the same reason

broadly, universally — 汎愛衆 is 汎く衆を愛し, which is the reading kanbun has always given this character in front of a verb. **The entry exists to be reached, not only to be right**: 汎愛 is a JMdict headword (はんあい) and 汎 stands as an adverbial `mod` directly on 愛, which is the very shape `oneLexicalWordPair` fuses — the 大破敵軍 shape — so both panels drew 汎愛 as one word and the prose read 衆を汎愛し. A conditioned curated entry is what stands that rule down (`curatedInRole`), and this one earns the stand-down on its own terms: 汎 in the adverbial slot is a word and not half of one, and 論語 學而 6 reads 汎く衆を愛して仁に親しみ. Split ひろ + く on the model of 遂 つひ + に — KANJIDIC2 dots the character's kun at ひろ.い, so ひろ is the character's own reading and く the 連用形 ending that stands beside it. **Measured** over `lzh_kyoto-sud-{train,dev,test}.relabeled_ext.udep_ruled.punct.rulemerged.adjfix.conllu`: 汎 is 6 tokens in all — 3 ADV, every one of them `mod` and both 汎愛 pairs among them, and 3 VERB, which go on reading ただよう through KANJIDIC2 exactly as before. The tag is what separates the adverb from the verb here, as it already does for 遂 and 惟

entirely, all (ADV+mod: 悉 is also the verb "to know/exhaust in full" — 悉其力 came out その力をことごとく. The dep is needed as well as the POS because the parser tags that verb ADV as readily as VERB (書不能悉意 is ADV+comp:aux, 其悉朽意 is ADV+ROOT), while every adverbial use checked (悉如外人, 悉知其情, 悉召群臣, 兵甲悉具) is ADV+mod)

together (a split reading, the same one 其 takes as そ+の and 輒 as すなは+ち: とも is the character's own reading and goes over it, に is the adverbial particle and sits beside it as okurigana. 倶ニ, not 倶(トモニ) with the whole word in the okurigana slot). No context gate, unlike 其/何: those each have a distinct non-attributive sense for a gate to separate (それ, なに/なんぞ), and this character has only the one sense in kanbun — a gate would narrow the entry's reach without distinguishing anything. It would also make the entry role-qualified, which vetoes the on'yomi pair rule (see `curatedInRole`), and this character's Sino-Japanese pairs are exactly what that rule is for
together (= 倶; the variant form U+4FF1, which is what the texts use — 俱言不須)

increasingly, more and more (ADV+mod: 益 is also the verb 益す "to increase" and the noun "benefit" — 曾益其所不能 and 有益於人 both came out ますます. The dep is needed as well as the POS: the parser tags the 益 of the compound 損益 ADV too, but as comp:obj, where every adverbial use it was checked against (如水益深, 秦益輕趙, 兵益進, 老當益壯) is ADV+mod. parataxis is the second adverbial dep and was added on a live parse: 適以益貧 hangs 益 off the preceding clause as parataxis with 貧 as its own comp:obl, and with mod alone the entry did not match at all — 益 fell to KANJIDIC2's ま.す and printed 益すて. Listed rather than the restriction being dropped, because what the dep is really excluding is comp:obj, and findOverride can only name the deps an entry admits)

it...at (fusion of 之於/之乎) — 諸を枉れるに錯く. Divided これ + を: the を is the 於 half of the fusion rather than part of the word, so it belongs beside the character, which is where the received text puts it (諸を 34 times in the gold). The split also brings the token under `ownReadingSuppliesCaseParticle`, so the slot's own を is not written a second time
and that is all (= 耳, fixed phrase)
and that is all (fixed closing phrase)

to be so, thus (ADJ beside VERB since parser 0.3.2, which recodes the stative class off VERB: over the recoded gold 然 is ADV 442 / ADJ 303 / PART 215 and VERB 0, so a VERB-only condition would match nothing the parser can now produce and every predicative 然 would lose its しかり)
only after that, and then (= 然後)

or perhaps; now then (ADV-only: 抑 is also the ordinary verb 拑ふ "to suppress", which this parser tags VERB — 抑其心 came out その心をそもそも. No dep condition: the adverb is tagged mod before a following clause (抑亦可以為次矣) but ROOT when it opens the sentence outright (抑王興甲兵))
rather — 寧ろ竈に媚びよ. Divided むし + ろ, as the received text writes it (寧ろ 4 times in the gold)
it would be better to, not as good as
not (= 不, often with transitive verbs)
there is not (= 無) (ADV-only: 罔 is also the verb しいる "to ensnare, to delude" — 是罔民也 came out 民をなし)
once, formerly (ADV-only: 嘗 is also the verb なめむ "to taste", tagged VERB — 嘗其肉而知其味 came out その肉をかつてて…)
in the end, finally (ADV-only: 竟 is also the verb おはる "to finish", tagged VERB — 竟其業 came out その業をつひに)

as expected, sure enough (the adverb 果たして, split at its conventional okurigana boundary the way 以's もつ+て is. VERB as well as ADV, and the dep is what carries the condition: this treebank tags the adverb VERB as readily as ADV — 果然 comes back VERB/mod with ExtPos=VERB — while 果 the verb は(た)す "to carry out, to come to an end" is a predicate and stands as ROOT/comp:obj/conj:coord, never as mod. Standing before its predicate is what makes it the adverb, and 果然 is read はたして然り in kundoku, not the Sino-Japanese かぜん JMdict lists. ADJ joins the two since parser 0.3.2: 果 in that use carries the `v,動詞,描写,態度` xpos, and the recoding moves that whole class off VERB, so the mod-standing 果然 the entry names now arrives ADJ)
happen to, at that time (= 會)
my (attributive genitive on `det` — 朕躬有罪 -> 朕が躬に罪有り). Split わ + が on 其's そ + の model; the whole argument, the relation, and the gold counts are on the 吾 entry above

now, (sentence-initial topic-introducing particle). Written 夫れ and not それ: `spellOutInProse` is false here as it is on every other それ/これ entry in this table (其 それ, 其 そ+の, 是 これ, 之 これ, 諸 これ+を), and 夫 was the one that was not. Counted rather than assumed — over the whole kanbun.info corpus (178,468 characters of received 書き下し文) the kana それ and これ appear **zero** times between them, while the characters are kept throughout: 其の 1,412, 其れ 104, 之 1,491, 是れ 130, 此れ 129 and 夫れ 147. The reading it divides by is the one `READING_ENDING_SPLITS` in classicalEnding.ts already states for それ, so 夫れ falls out of the same rule 其れ does and nothing is asserted twice. Reachable at all only since the two panels stopped taking bare `discourse` into their sentence-final-particle branch: 夫 is PART/`discourse` in 499 of its gold tokens and PART/`discourse@sp` in 29, and for the first group this entry was never reached at all — both panels took the discourse branch first and wrote SENTENCE_FINAL_PARTICLES’ かな, which is 夫’s *other* word. See `isSentenceFinalParticleUse` in conjugationContext.ts. The かな half is untouched and lives in SENTENCE_FINAL_PARTICLES — one character, two words, and the relation is what tells them apart

in general, all, on the whole. A split reading, the same one 以 takes as もつ+て and 乃 as すなは+ち: およ is the character's own reading — KANJIDIC2 files 凡 as およ.そ and the dot is the division — and そ sits beside it in the okurigana slot. `spellOutInProse: false` is what keeps the character in the 書き下し文: over kanbun.info's whole prose 凡そ stands 146 times and およそ in kana none, and the app was printing the kana on all of them

just like (re-read: なホ…ガごとシ; = 猶) (ADV-only, and this is the rarer sense of the two: 由 is far more often the adposition "from, by way of" (由此觀之, 由是觀之 — tagged ADP) or the verb "to follow, to proceed from" (必由之, 言不由衷 — tagged VERB), and unconditioned this re-read claimed all of them. The 猶 sense is tagged ADV (王由足用為善). Note that 由 as an adposition then falls through to kanjidic's よし rather than the より it wants — a separate gap, not one this table can close)
